name: Park Guell
_about: PARK GUELL, Barcelona (Antoni Gaudi, 1900-1914): the main entrance of Eusebi Guell's garden city on the Muntanya Pelada -- the rubble wall with its medallions, the two gingerbread pavilions (the porter's lodge with its amanita, the administration with its chequered hyperboloid tower and four-armed cross), the double stair round the trencadis dragon, the hypostyle room of 86 Doric columns under shallow white vaults and Jujol's rosettes, the oval square on it edged by the serpentine bench, and the washerwoman's portico of leaning columns. Built by tools/archgen/park_guell.py from gaudi.py's components.

vestibule._about: the vestibule inside the gate, 400 m2 between the pavilions and the stair, paved

street._about: Carrer d'Olot in front of the wall

west wall._about: the wall round the park (210 m of it built), of the hill's own stone laid rough, 2-4 m high

west wall crest._about: its crest, rolled and dressed in trencadis in bands of white and red

east wall._about: the wall round the park (210 m of it built), of the hill's own stone laid rough, 2-4 m high

east wall crest._about: its crest, rolled and dressed in trencadis in bands of white and red

medallions._about: the 15 medallions on the street face, 1.4 m across, 'Park' and 'Guell' in trencadis (sourced number and size; their spacing estimated)

gate._about: the wrought-iron gate's two leaves, swung back against the pavilions' ends: uprights, rails, and the fan of a palm leaf in each

porter's lodge._about: the porter's lodge (now the park's interpretation centre): 14.80 x 7.66 m, two floors and the attic in the roof, the tower with its mirador and the amanita to 21 m

administration._about: the administration pavilion (now the shop): 12.60 x 6.60 m, two floors, its mushroom cupola, and at its street corner the hyperboloid tower in a white and blue chequer, the cross on it at 29 m

spine 2._about: the spine between the branches, stepping up with them: a fountain's basin at each level

spine 4._about: the spine between the branches, stepping up with them: a fountain's basin at each level

basins._about: the fountains' basins: the grotto's at the foot, the coat of arms' with its snake, and the one the dragon spits into

grotto._about: the first fountain: a grotto of the hill's rough stones, the water welling from it into the basin

coat of arms._about: the second fountain: the four bars of the Catalan arms on the spine's face, in trencadis

snake._about: the snake's head over the arms, the water from its mouth (the serpent of Asclepius, or the Python of Delphi)

dragon head._about: its head and upper jaw, eyes bulging

dragon jaw._about: its lower jaw dropped: the open mouth the water runs from

dragon crest._about: the ridge of plates along its back, from the head to the tail

odeon bench._about: the little odeon on the spine's last step: a curved bench facing the street, sheltered from the wind, in the sun (sourced; its size estimated)

stair wall west._about: the stair's side wall, close along its flights and splaying out at the foot, its face a chequer of white and coloured trencadis

planter west._about: the planter trough along the wall's top, in trencadis

stair merlons west._about: the rounded merlons along the wall's inner edge, over the stair

bed west._about: the planted bank behind the stair's wall, falling to the vestibule

stair wall east._about: the stair's side wall, close along its flights and splaying out at the foot, its face a chequer of white and coloured trencadis

stair merlons east._about: the rounded merlons along the wall's inner edge, over the stair

bed east._about: the planted bank behind the stair's wall, falling to the vestibule

front columns._about: the front row: inclined, feet out, along the line of the vaults' push

west columns._about: the west file: inclined, feet out, along the line of the vaults' push

east columns._about: the east file: inclined, feet out, along the line of the vaults' push

hypostyle fill._about: the ground under the hall's floor

floor._about: the hall's floor, where the market was to be

vaults._about: the ceiling: a shallow cupola over every bay, column to column, in white trencadis

ceiling._about: the band of ceiling round the vaults, from the outer columns to the walls

rosettes._about: Jujol's rosettes, 3 m across, where columns were left out: suns of twenty points, the seasons

side walls._about: the side walls of rubble against the earth

back wall._about: the back wall against the hill

corner walls._about: the front corners cut on the diagonal: the hall is square but for its chamfers on the stair side

architrave._about: the front's architrave over the inclined columns

triglyphs._about: the triglyphs on the frieze, one over each column and one between

gargoyles._about: lion-head gargoyles spouting the square's rain from its cornice (sourced; spacing estimated)

square._about: the Nature Square (the Greek theatre), 86 x 43 m, the stage for the colony's fiestas; its gravel drains into the columns

west terrace._about: the square's end beyond the hypostyle, carried on the hill and its own retaining wall of rubble

east terrace._about: the square's end beyond the hypostyle, carried on the hill and its own retaining wall of rubble

back terrace._about: the square's back edge beyond the hall, on the hill

bench._about: the serpentine bench round the square's edge (Gaudi and Jujol, 1910-1914): its back rolls over like a wave, its loops make little rooms; white trencadis below, every colour above

hill._about: the Muntanya Pelada behind the square, rising west toward the Turo de les Tres Creus, its south flank carrying the portico (its shape estimated)

west slope._about: the hillside either side of the stair and the square, gardens climbing from the street (estimated)

east slope._about: the hillside either side of the stair and the square, gardens climbing from the street (estimated)

portico ground._about: portico: the terrace it stands on

portico wall._about: the retaining wall, its open face battered back as it rises, rubble

portico bank._about: the hillside the wall holds back

portico outer columns._about: the outer file: upright, rough-hewn, swelling at the foot like palms

portico inner columns._about: the inner file, leaning back toward the wall: Gaudi's columns take the push of the earth on their slant

portico parapet._about: a low parapet along the open edge
